tagline: Last Almaz military station — Soyuz 21 + Soyuz 24 crews; Soyuz 23 failed approach; reentered 1977-08-08 after 412 days
dispatch: Salyut 5 was the last of the Almaz military stations, flown in 1976 under the usual civilian disguise. Two crews were sent: the first, Soyuz 21, was evacuated early amid reports of a foul odour and a stressed crew; the second, Soyuz 24, completed a normal stay. Soon after, automated reconnaissance satellites had improved to the point that cosmonauts with cameras were no longer worth the risk, and the military Almaz line was quietly retired — leaving the future to the civilian stations.
description: The third and last Soviet military Almaz station. Launched 1976-06-22 on a Proton-K, Salyut 5 hosted two crews: Soyuz 21 (Volynov + Zholobov, 49 days, 1976-07-06 to 1976-08-24 — cut short by acrid odours the crew traced to a corroded film-return capsule seal) and Soyuz 24 (Gorbatko + Glazkov, 17 days, 1977-02-07 to 1977-02-25 — first cosmonauts to swap a station's atmosphere through vent + recharge). Soyuz 23 (Zudov + Rozhdestvensky, 1976-10-14) failed to dock after the Igla rendezvous system malfunctioned; the crew survived a high-water splashdown in Lake Tengiz, the only Soviet water landing. Salyut 5 was the last Almaz mission flown — the program was cancelled after the station deorbited on 1977-08-08.
